data.body:
CLOSE EVIDENCE — landed as Gerrit change 2153, merged to main as b04405e20d (LLM-Review +1 rebar review bot, Verified +1 rebar CI bot via run 32621957242, 0 unresolved comments).

What landed:
- .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml: removed the CLI `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` flags from BOTH shared-tier lanes (default-suite and integration; `--max-worker-restart=0` kept on the integration lane); comment blocks rewritten to state the lanes are flag-free on purpose (pytest-timeout precedence CLI > ini + trusted-main workflow execution = permanent shadowing, bug 3fa7-94ba-42aa-4623 / change 2115 PS1).
- tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py: shared-tier contract is now test_the_shared_tier_lanes_are_flag_free_and_governed_by_the_ini (asserts zero --timeout/--timeout-method matches on both lanes); the hang-guard sweep asserts the ini carries timeout>0 + thread method and exempts ONLY flag-free _build-and-test.yml lanes — every other workflow's calibrated lanes still must carry explicit flags.
- docs/local-dev-env.md: lanes documented as flag-free/single-sourced (no floor section).

Effective budget before/after: UNCHANGED (CLI 300/thread -> ini 300/thread; only the authority moved to pyproject.toml).

Branch mining/deletion: preserve/timeout-floor-hardening (b38bf9a4748) was mined for its parity-test rewrites and lane-flag removals; its conftest-floor mechanism was rejected (pytest-timeout resolves config._env_timeout at session start — no supported hook point, no OSS precedent). The branch existed ONLY locally (git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/preserve/*' returned nothing), so it was deleted with a local branch -D; no origin push needed.

Caused-by: 89d5-61da-b621-47f8 — its commit f47acb7051 introduced the CLI --timeout flags on these lanes (change 2115 / bug 3fa7 later restored the same pattern, but the lineage starts at 89d5).
